subject: business-studies
title: STP and Product Life Cycle
welcome_lead: Segment, target, position - then ride the life cycle from launch to decline.
meta_desc: A-Level Marketing: STP and the four product life cycle stages.
final_note: Position deliberately, then manage each life cycle stage with a different marketing mix.

concepts.def: Dividing a market into groups with similar needs.
Designing the offer to occupy a clear place in customers' minds.
Life cycle stage of launch - low sales, high marketing spend.
Sales rising quickly, profits emerging, rivals enter.
Sales peak then fall; extension strategies can prolong life.

walkthroughs.body_html: Segmentation uses demographic, geographic, psychographic or behavioural criteria. Targeting picks attractive segments. Positioning crafts perception - Volvo means safety, BMW means performance.
Most products move from introduction through growth, maturity and decline. Each stage needs different pricing, promotion and channels - heavy launch ads in introduction, repositioning in maturity.
Firms delay decline through extension strategies: new flavours, new markets, repackaging, or repositioning. Lucozade moved from medicinal drink to sports drink and gained decades of growth.

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A brand is just the logo on a product.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Ansoff's Matrix shows market share against profit.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
